newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-KILMARNOCK SEND RANGERS STUMBLING TO DEFEAT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KILMARNOCK SEND RANGERS STUMBLING TO DEFEAT.

text.p: Rangers' faltering progress to their ninth successive Scottish League title took another knock on Saturday when they were beaten 2-1 at home by Kilmarnock.
But Old Firm rivals Celtic, the only team who can catch them, failed to exact maximum advantage, dropping two points in a 2-2 draw at Dunfermline.

Rangers, who moved eight points clear of Celtic after beating them 1-0 last week, have now won only one of their last five matches and were chasing this one after Jim McIntyre put Kilmarnock ahead after 38 minutes.
Gordon Durie, recovered from the stomach upset which kept him out of the side which played Celtic last week, tapped home an equaliser from six metres after 53 minutes.
But Kilmarnock, who beat Celtic recently, completed a successful Old Firm double with their fourth sucessive victory after Paul Wright's successful 81st-minute penalty.

Mid-table Dunfermline were 2-0 up against Celtic after only 29 minutes through Gerry Britton and Harry Curran but Celtic fought back in the second half with goals from Phil O'Donnell and Simon Donnelly.

Third-placed Dundee United stretched their unbeaten run to 17 matches with a 2-1 home win over bottom club Raith, whose relegation is now looking certain. Robbie Winters was United's hero with a goal in each half.
